title: Microfluidic platform for spatially segregated experimental evolution studies with E. coli
protocol: Streak −80°C frozen stock containing strains of interest onto non-selective, nutrient-rich agar plates.
Incubate plates aerobically for 1 day at 37°C.
Select a single colony using a sterile loop or swab.
Add the selected colony to each test tube containing 5 or 10 mL of sterile growth media.
Incubate in a shaker at 250 rpm at 37°C.
Measure OD600 values of cultures.
Convert OD600 values to CFU counts/mL using a standard curve.
Dilute cultures with fresh growth media to achieve the desired lambda (λ).
Prepare at least four populations of 2 mL growth media containing the desired number of cells in 50-mL conical-bottom tubes.
Maintain the same λ value during experimental evolution.

Calculate the average number of cells per microdroplet using the Poisson distribution formula P(X = x) = λxe-λ/x!, where P is the probability, x is the number of cells, and λ is the average number of cells per microdroplet.
At the end of the experiment, perform deep sequencing of the entire population.
Identify genes associated with resistance to antibiotics.
Transfer each prepared population to a 3-mL sterile syringe in a biosafety cabinet.
Prepare six 3-mL sterile syringes containing 2 mL of fluorinated oil with 1.5% (wt/wt) fluorinated surfactants.
Affix one end of PTFE tubing to a sterile syringe needle and another one to the inlet of the PDMS microdroplets generator.
Load twelve 3-mL sterile syringes to a twelve-channel programmable syringe pump.
Start infusing with 100 μL min-1 of both flow rates for cell suspension and the continuous oil phase.
Confirm the size of microdroplets under the microscope before operation in a biosafety cabinet.
Record highly homogeneous microdroplets with a high-speed camera attached to an inverted microscope with a 10× objective lens.
Use ImageJ software for analyses of microdroplet diameters.
Collect microscopy images of more than 50 microdroplets.
Calculate the diameters of microdroplets using their projected areas.
Create histograms of the microdroplet diameters for evaluation.
Determine average diameter values with standard deviations by fitting Gaussian or Lorentzian models to the histograms.
Collect approximately 2.0 mL of emulsions (1.0 mL of microdroplets) into a 50-mL conical-bottom tube for 10 minutes.
Incubate microdroplets containing E. coli at 37°C for 24 hours.
Carefully transfer approximately 1.0 mL of microdroplets from an old 50-mL conical-bottom tube to a new 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube using a pipette.
Filter sterilize fluorinated oil containing 1.5 w/w% fluorinated surfactants through a 0.22 μm filter for recycling.
Use a sterile capillary tube to take microscopy images of microdroplets after incubation.
Add 250 μl of 1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluoro-1-octanol (PFO) to 1.0 ml of microdroplets.
Gently mix the contents by tapping a 1.5-ml Eppendorf tube with a finger for 30 seconds.
Leave the tubes in a biosafety cabinet for 5–10 minutes.
Pipette 100 μl of growth media containing E. coli into each well of flat-bottom 96-well microplates.
Measure OD600 values of six populations using a microplate reader.
Calculate volumes required for the desired λ in the next iteration.
Repeat steps with gradually increasing antibiotic concentration until it reaches four-fold of the antibiotic’s clinical breakpoint.
When the density of E. coli is 1.71×10^8 CFU/mL after incubation, use ∼1.5% dilution factor to get 2.6×10^6 CFU/mL of the starting population for the next iteration.
Mix 200 μL of collected cell suspension with 66.7 μl of 80% (vol/vol) sterile glycerol (20% final concentration).
Prepare two glycerol stock solutions for each population, one for daily deep metagenomic sequencing from whole-community samples and another for storage.
Store the glycerol stock solutions at -80°C.

On the last day of experimental evolution when the concentration of antibiotics has reached the target maximum concentration, spread each population onto non-selective, nutrient-rich agar plates for the selection of evolved isolates following appropriate dilution.
Randomly select a single colony to add to each test tube containing 5 or 10 mL of sterile growth media using a sterile loop or swab.
Perform Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) test for endpoint isolates.
Prepare two glycerol stock solutions for each endpoint isolate.
Store glycerol stock solutions at -80°C.
